identity.title: The Eccentric Cavity, Triple Rings, Two-armed Spirals, and Double Clumps of the MWC 758 Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA dust continuum observations of MWC 758 at 0.87 millimeter (mm) wavelength with 43$\times$39 mas angular resolution (6.9$\times$6.2 AU) and 20 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ rms.

evidence.quote: MWC 758 is a 3.5$\pm$2 Myr (cite: meeus12) Herbig Ae star located at a distance of 160$\pm$2 pc (cite: gaia18).

question.value: What is the high-resolution sub-mm dust structure of the MWC 758 disk (cavity, rings, spirals, clumps), and what does it imply about unseen companions?

evidence.quote: Previous imaging observations of the transitional disk around MWC 758 revealed an inner cavity, a ring-like outer disk, emission clumps, and spiral arms, all possibly generated by companions.
were carried out in Cycle 5 by ALMA under the project 2017.1.00492.S.

The first EB was conducted on 2017 November 12 with 48 antennas in the array configuration C43-8.
The combined dataset has baselines ranging between 92 m and 11.84 km
This results in a synthesized beam size of 43$\times$39 mas (6.8$\times$6.2 AU) at PA=-4.3$^\circ$
a rms noise level of 20 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$
The total integration time on-source is about 125 minutes.
The other two EBs were conducted on 2017 November 25 with 48 and 49 antennas
